_1_what_this_is: The character bible. This file is the single source of truth for the project.
build_project.py reads it and emits every per-character card list from these rows,
so the IDENTITY and WARDROBE lists that appear in BOTH phases cannot drift apart.
Never hand-edit 'Podcast Auditions.json'. Edit this, then re-run build_project.py.
_2_todo_ned: EVERY 'characters' row below is PLACEHOLDER. All of it must be replaced.
The placeholders are deliberately ugly so nobody mistakes them for finished copy.
'seed' is the one field that does NOT need replacing — see the field notes.
_3_row_count: The number of rows here sets the loop count in both phases. Six is the design,
but any count works as long as every row is complete. Add or remove whole rows;
do not leave a row half-filled.

_4_fields.name: Internal label only. Never reaches the model. Used in verify_project.py's report.
_4_fields.identity: One clause. Build, age, face, hair. Reads after 'a headshot ... of '. No trailing period, no leading space.
_4_fields.wardrobe: One clause. Reads after ', wearing '. No trailing period, no leading space.
_4_fields.slate: SPOKEN. The character naming themselves and the role. Written WITHOUT quotation marks — build_project.py adds them.
_4_fields.line: SPOKEN. The second beat. Also written WITHOUT quotation marks.
_4_fields.voice: One clause. Reads after ' in '. Describes delivery, not content. No trailing period.
_4_fields.seed: Integer, pinned so a rejected anchor can be regenerated identically. Arbitrary values are fine; these ship usable. Not a TODO.

_5_hard_rules: NO double-quote characters (") anywhere in any field. framesDialog sizes the clip by counting
words inside "..." spans, and build_project.py owns those spans. A stray quote in your text
splits a span and silently changes the frame count. verify_project.py fails on this.
slate + line together must be 20 SPOKEN WORDS OR FEWER. At wps 2.6 / padding 48, 20 words is
249 frames; 22 words is 265, which is past Tanque Studio's 257-frame cap while StoryflowPipeline.js
has no cap at all — so past 20 words the two engines silently render different lengths.
verify_project.py prints the per-character frame count and flags anything over 257.
